title: Architecture analysis: Build-time dependency installation via build_commands in repositories.yaml
summary: Add a `build_commands` configuration section to per-repo settings in `repositories.yaml` that allows users to specify dependency installation commands (e.g. `npm ci`, `pip install -r requirements.txt`) to run during the Docker image build phase. Watch files (e.g. lockfiles) are copied into the build context to enable Docker layer caching — deps only rebuild when watch files change. All repos' dependencies coexist in the single `egg` image. The recommended approach extends the existing `docker-setup.py` build script to handle `build_commands` for each repo, adds a new Dockerfile layer that copies watch files before running the build script, and extends `compute_build_hash()` to include watch file contents.

problem_statement.description: In private mode, the sandbox container has no network access beyond the Anthropic API. Dependencies cannot be installed at runtime — pip install, npm install, etc. all fail. The existing `docker_setup.extra_packages` config only supports OS-level apt/dnf packages during image build. There is no mechanism for project-specific dependency installation (Python venvs, node_modules, Go modules) that requires repo-specific files like lockfiles or Makefiles.
constraints: All dependencies must be baked into the single `egg` Docker image — no per-repo images
Docker layer caching must be leveraged so dependency layers are only rebuilt when watch files change
Only watch files (not full repos) are copied during build — full repos are mounted at runtime
Backwards compatible — repos without `build_commands` are unaffected
Commands run as root during build, same as existing `docker-setup.py` execution context
Must work with the existing build hash system to detect when rebuilds are needed
Watch file paths must be validated to prevent path traversal outside the repo directory

current_architecture.build_pipeline_overview: The Docker build pipeline is orchestrated by `sandbox/egg_lib/docker.py`. The `build_image()` function checks `should_rebuild_image()` (using content hashing), then calls `create_dockerfile()` to stage files into `~/.cache/egg/`, and finally runs `docker build`. The `compute_build_hash()` function hashes all build-affecting files to determine if a rebuild is needed. The hash is stored as a Docker image label (`org.egg.build-hash`).

key_components.name: compute_build_hash()
key_components.description: Computes SHA256 of all build-affecting files including Dockerfile, entrypoint.py, docker-setup.py, pyproject.toml, and all runtime directories. Includes UID/GID. Does NOT currently include any config files or repo-specific files.

key_components.name: create_dockerfile()
key_components.description: Stages build context into ~/.cache/egg/. Copies sandbox files (docker-setup.py, claude-commands, claude-rules, runtime dirs, entrypoint.py, Dockerfile) and shared/ directory. Uses _copy_directory_atomic() with retry logic for race-condition safety. Does NOT currently copy any repo-specific files.

key_components.name: build_image()
key_components.description: Orchestrates the full build: checks if rebuild needed, calls create_dockerfile(), computes hash, runs docker build with build args (USER_NAME, USER_UID, USER_GID, CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION) and labels.

key_components.name: docker-setup.py
key_components.description: Build-time script that installs core + extra OS packages. Reads repositories.yaml for docker_setup.extra_packages. Runs as root during docker build. Has load_config(), get_extra_packages(), install_core_packages(), install_extra_packages(), and configure_system() functions. Called from Dockerfile lines 58-63.

key_components.name: Dockerfile
key_components.description: Ubuntu 22.04 base. Layer order: core utils (7-31) → gh CLI (33-39) → Python 3.11 (41-53) → pyyaml (55-56) → docker-setup.py for OS packages (58-63) → core Python deps (65-77) → PyPI pre-installs (79-104) → Claude commands/rules (110-118) → user creation (120-131) → Claude Code CLI (133-148) → runtime COPY (150-161) → git/gh relocation (163-170) → PYTHONPATH (172-174) → entrypoint (176-182). The docker-setup.py layer is near the top for caching stability.

key_components.name: get_local_repos()
key_components.description: Returns list of Path objects from local_repos.paths in repositories.yaml. Used by container setup to mount repos. We need this to locate repo directories from which to copy watch files.

key_components.name: get_repo_setting()
key_components.description: Generic per-repo setting accessor. Looks up repo_settings[repo][setting] with case-insensitive repo matching. Can be used to retrieve build_commands.

approaches.name: Extend docker-setup.py to handle build_commands (Recommended)
approaches.description: Extend the existing docker-setup.py build-time script to also read and execute `build_commands` from a build-commands.json manifest. Watch files are copied into the build context by `create_dockerfile()` from local repo paths. A NEW Dockerfile layer (after the existing docker-setup.py layer and all toolchain installations) COPYs the watch files and manifest, then runs `docker-setup.py --build-commands` as a second invocation. The first docker-setup.py invocation (line 58-63) remains unchanged, preserving cache for OS packages.

Extend to hash watch file contents from the build context (repo-deps/ directory) and the build_commands config (serialized JSON)

Add --build-commands CLI flag, install_build_commands() function that reads the manifest, and get_build_commands() to parse it. When invoked with --build-commands, ONLY runs build commands (not OS packages).

Add a new layer after the PyPI pre-installs (after line 104) that: (1) COPYs repo-deps/ to /tmp/repo-deps/, (2) COPYs build-commands.json to /tmp/, (3) COPYs docker-setup.py again, (4) RUNs docker-setup.py --build-commands && rm docker-setup.py build-commands.json. This is a SECOND invocation of docker-setup.py, separate from the existing one at line 58-63.
Document the build_commands feature and its caching behavior

pros: Minimally invasive — extends existing patterns (docker-setup.py already reads config and installs packages)
Docker layer caching works naturally — watch files are COPYd before RUN, so Docker only rebuilds when files change
Existing docker-setup.py layer (OS packages) is completely unchanged — cache preserved
The second invocation is a clean separation: OS packages vs project dependencies
No new scripts or binaries needed
Build hash system naturally extends to include watch files
cons: docker-setup.py grows in complexity (but still manageable at ~350 lines total)
Watch file resolution requires mapping repo name to local path, which means create_dockerfile() needs to read config
docker-setup.py is COPYd twice in the Dockerfile (once for OS packages, once for build commands)

approaches.name: New dedicated build-deps.py script
approaches.description: Create a new sandbox/build-deps.py script specifically for project-level dependency installation. This script would be separate from docker-setup.py (which stays focused on OS packages). The Dockerfile would have a dedicated layer that runs build-deps.py after docker-setup.py.
pros: Clean separation of concerns — OS packages vs project dependencies
cons: Adds a new file to maintain
Duplicates config loading logic from docker-setup.py
Slightly more Dockerfile complexity (another COPY + RUN layer)

approaches.name: Dynamic Dockerfile generation with per-repo COPY+RUN layers
approaches.description: Instead of a static Dockerfile, dynamically generate Dockerfile content in create_dockerfile() that includes per-repo COPY and RUN instructions.
cons: Significantly more complex — Dockerfile becomes dynamically generated
Harder to debug (generated Dockerfiles are opaque)
Breaks the current pattern of static Dockerfile copied to build context
Over-engineering for the typical 1-3 repos case

recommendation_justification: Approach A extends existing patterns with minimal complexity. The docker-setup.py script already reads repositories.yaml and installs packages — adding build_commands handling is a natural extension. Docker layer caching still works well because all watch files are COPYd in a single layer before the RUN. For the typical 1-3 repos case, the cache invalidation difference vs. per-repo layers (Approach C) is negligible, and the simplicity advantage is significant. Approach B is reasonable but creates unnecessary separation for what is conceptually the same operation (installing things at build time).

tasks.title: Copy watch files into build context with path traversal validation
tasks.description: Extend create_dockerfile() to: (1) read build_commands config for all repos, (2) resolve each repo name to a local path via local_repos.paths (matching by repo name == directory name), (3) VALIDATE that all watch_files paths, after resolution against the repo's local directory, remain within that directory using Path.resolve() and is_relative_to(repo_base_path) — reject paths that escape with a clear error, (4) copy each repo's validated watch_files from the local path into ~/.cache/egg/repo-deps/<repo-name>/, (5) generate a build-commands.json manifest with explicit field allowlisting (repo name, commands, workdir only — no other repo_settings fields). Handle missing watch files gracefully (warn but don't fail). Use _copy_directory_atomic() or equivalent atomic pattern for race-condition safety.
tasks.design_notes: PATH TRAVERSAL VALIDATION (R-6, DD-8): For each watch_file path, compute `(repo_local_path / watch_file).resolve()` and verify `resolved.is_relative_to(repo_local_path.resolve())`. If a path escapes (e.g., '../../etc/passwd'), reject it with a clear error message naming the offending path and repo. Also reject paths containing null bytes. MANIFEST SECURITY (R-3, DD-6): The build-commands.json manifest must be constructed by explicitly selecting only {repo_name, watch_files, commands} — use an allowlist, not a denylist.

tasks.title: Extend build hash to include watch files and build_commands config
tasks.description: Extend compute_build_hash() to: (1) hash the contents of all watch files copied to the build context (repo-deps/ directory), (2) hash the build_commands configuration itself (serialized as stable JSON — sorted keys). This ensures that changes to either the watch files or the commands trigger a rebuild.

tasks.title: Extend docker-setup.py to execute build_commands via --build-commands flag
tasks.description: Add a --build-commands CLI flag to docker-setup.py. When invoked with this flag, the script ONLY runs build commands (not OS packages). Add get_build_commands() function that reads /tmp/build-commands.json manifest. Add install_build_commands(entries) function that iterates entries, cd's to workdir, and runs each command via subprocess.run(shell=True, check=False) with logging. Log failures prominently. Print summary at end. The main() function dispatches based on --build-commands flag.
tasks.design_notes: The --build-commands flag creates a clean dispatch: FIRST invocation (Dockerfile line 58-63) runs without flag → OS packages. SECOND invocation (new layer) runs with --build-commands → project dependencies. Existing code path is unchanged.

tasks.title: Add Dockerfile layer for repo dependency installation
tasks.description:
Add a new layer to the Dockerfile after the PyPI pre-installs (after line 104, before Claude commands COPY at line 110). Exact Dockerfile addition:

# --- Phase: Project dependency installation (build_commands) ---
COPY sandbox/repo-deps/ /tmp/repo-deps/
COPY sandbox/build-commands.json /tmp/build-commands.json
COPY sandbox/docker-setup.py /tmp/docker-setup.py
RUN python3 /tmp/docker-setup.py --build-commands \
    && rm -f /tmp/docker-setup.py /tmp/build-commands.json

This is a SECOND invocation of docker-setup.py. The existing invocation at lines 58-63 is unchanged.
tasks.design_notes: docker-setup.py is COPYd twice intentionally: once for the OS package layer (stable cache), once for the build-commands layer (changes when deps change). Two separate cache layers with different invalidation triggers. If no repos have build_commands, the repo-deps/ and manifest are empty — the layer is a fast no-op.

design_decisions.question: How to map repo names to local paths for watch file copying
design_decisions.decision: Match the repo name (part after '/') against local_repos.paths directory names. For 'your-org/web-app', look for a directory named 'web-app' in local_repos.paths. If multiple matches exist, use the first. If no match, skip with a prominent warning including the repo name and paths searched.
design_decisions.rationale: Simplest approach for the common case. Directory names conventionally match the repo name.
alternatives_considered: Add an explicit local_path to repo_settings — more explicit but adds config burden
Use git remote to match — requires git access during build which isn't available

design_decisions.question: Where do dependency artifacts go (node_modules, venv, etc.)
design_decisions.decision: Dependencies install to system-global paths during build. pip install goes to system site-packages. npm ci warms the npm cache. Document the pip vs npm asymmetry and the --prefer-offline pattern for npm.
design_decisions.rationale: Repos are mounted at runtime, not during build. pip works naturally (system site-packages). npm requires cache-warming + runtime --prefer-offline.
design_decisions.note: Key UX consideration: document that build_commands operate in a directory with ONLY the watch files (CC-1).

design_decisions.question: Should build_commands failure be fatal?
design_decisions.decision: Default to non-fatal (warn and continue). Log failures prominently with command, exit code, and stderr. Print summary at end listing all failed commands.
design_decisions.rationale: Consistent with existing extra_packages behavior (check=False). Prominent logging addresses R-5.

design_decisions.question: Where to place the new Dockerfile layer
design_decisions.decision: After PyPI pre-installs (line 104), before Claude commands COPY (line 110).
design_decisions.rationale: All toolchains (Python, pip, and any extra_packages runtimes) are available. Maximizes cache reuse.

design_decisions.question: How to pass config to docker-setup.py for the build_commands phase
design_decisions.decision: Superseded by DD-6. Use the build-commands.json manifest approach.
design_decisions.rationale: repositories.yaml may not be at the standard path during docker build.

design_decisions.question: How to pass build_commands configuration into the Docker build
design_decisions.decision: Write a build-commands.json manifest containing ONLY {repo_name, watch_files, commands} per repo. Explicit field allowlisting — never serialize the full repo_settings. Manifest is deleted after the build layer (rm in the RUN command).
design_decisions.rationale: Avoids copying sensitive data from repositories.yaml into Docker image layers. Allowlist approach prevents accidental leakage.

design_decisions.question: How to structure the Dockerfile for build_commands execution
design_decisions.decision: Add a SECOND invocation of docker-setup.py with a --build-commands flag in a new Dockerfile layer. The existing docker-setup.py layer (lines 58-63, OS packages) is completely unchanged.
design_decisions.rationale: Cleanest approach: (1) existing OS package layer cache is fully preserved, (2) two invocations have different cache characteristics (OS packages rarely change; watch files change when deps update), (3) COPYing docker-setup.py again is standard Docker pattern for multi-use scripts, (4) --build-commands flag creates clean dispatch without affecting existing code path.
design_decisions.dockerfile_pseudocode:
# After line 104 (PyPI pre-installs), before line 110 (Claude commands):
# --- Project dependency installation (build_commands) ---
COPY sandbox/repo-deps/ /tmp/repo-deps/
COPY sandbox/build-commands.json /tmp/build-commands.json
COPY sandbox/docker-setup.py /tmp/docker-setup.py
RUN python3 /tmp/docker-setup.py --build-commands \
    && rm -f /tmp/docker-setup.py /tmp/build-commands.json

design_decisions.question: How to validate watch_files paths against path traversal
design_decisions.decision: For each watch_file path, compute (repo_local_path / watch_file).resolve() and verify resolved.is_relative_to(repo_local_path.resolve()). Reject paths that escape with a clear error. Also reject paths containing null bytes.
design_decisions.rationale: Standard path traversal prevention (R-6). Without validation, paths like '../../.ssh/id_rsa' could copy arbitrary host files into Docker image layers. is_relative_to() (Python 3.9+) is the canonical containment check.

risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: ADDRESSED IN REVISION 2. TASK-2 requires Path.resolve() + is_relative_to() validation for all watch_files paths. Paths escaping the repo directory are rejected with a clear error. DD-8 specifies the implementation pattern. TASK-6 includes path traversal test cases. Acceptance criteria for TASK-2: 'Watch file paths that escape the repo directory (e.g., ../../etc/passwd) are rejected with an error.'

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Sensitive data leakage via build-commands.json manifest (R-3)
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Manifest generation uses explicit field allowlisting: only {repo_name, watch_files, commands}. DD-6 specifies this. Code review should verify no other repo_settings fields leak.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Build commands may fail in the watch-file-only directory

risks_and_mitigations.risk: npm/node_modules artifacts lost at runtime mount (R-1)
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Document pip vs npm asymmetry. For npm, document cache-warming and --prefer-offline pattern.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Stale watch files if user forgets to rebuild
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Build hash system handles this automatically.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Build hash may miss command-only changes (R-7)
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Hash the full build_commands config as serialized JSON (sorted keys), not just watch file contents.
Log failures prominently with command, exit code, stderr. Print summary listing all failed commands.

risks_and_mitigations.risk: Concurrent egg instances race on build context (R-10)
risks_and_mitigations.mitigation: Use _copy_directory_atomic() or equivalent for watch file copying.

open_questions.question: Should npm dependencies be installed globally or should we use a persistent npm cache?
open_questions.context: npm ci installs to ./node_modules relative to the working directory. The build directory won't persist at runtime when the actual repo is mounted.
open_questions.recommendation: Option (b) — warm the npm cache. Run 'npm ci' during build to populate the cache. At runtime, 'npm ci --prefer-offline' reads from cache. Document this pattern clearly.

open_questions.context: docker-setup.py runs as root. Some package managers prefer non-root.
open_questions.recommendation: Start with root-only. Add run_as support later if requested.
